outcomesHub.metaTitle: What are you trying to achieve?
outcomesHub.metaDescription: Start with your objective, not our organisation chart. Six routes into EdCo.
outcomesHub.heroTitle: Start with your objective. Not our organisation chart.
outcomesHub.heroStandfirst: You don’t need to know which EdCo product or team you need. That’s our job.
outcomesHub.heroLead: Tell us what you’re trying to achieve. We’ll work out what combination of intelligence, people, technology and engagement capability makes sense.
outcomesHub.heading: Different problems need different answers.
outcomesHub.body: A marketing agency is likely to suggest marketing. A data provider is likely to suggest data. A software company is likely to suggest software.
outcomesHub.body2: That isn’t necessarily wrong. But it isn’t how we start.
outcomesHub.body3: Because sometimes the answer is a campaign. Sometimes it’s research. Sometimes it’s better intelligence. Sometimes it’s something useful to give educators. Sometimes it’s technology. Often it’s several things working together.
outcomesHub.heading2: Some things people actually say to us
outcomesHub.body4: None of these is a fixed process. They’re examples of how intelligence, people, content and engagement combine around an objective.

productsHub.metaDescription: Education IQ, the Engagement Hub, SPIRIT, the International Schools Network and The Curriculum Network — different ways of solving education-specific problems.
productsHub.heroStandfirst: They are part of EdCo, not separate businesses.
productsHub.heroLead: EdCo products are different ways of solving education-specific problems. Which of them is relevant depends entirely on what you’re trying to achieve.
productsHub.body: Your technology doesn’t need our logo on it.
productsHub.body2: If you already have a CRM you like — Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics or anything else — we’ll help make that environment more valuable. SPIRIT is an option, not an agenda.

capabilitiesHub.metaDescription: Research, marketing, events and CPD, content, data, technology, CSR programmes and education strategy — the capabilities behind the outcomes.
capabilitiesHub.heroStandfirst: Useful to know. Not the best place to start.
capabilitiesHub.heroLead: If you already know what you need, it’s all here. If you don’t, start with what you’re trying to achieve and let us do the diagnosis.
capabilitiesHub.body2: A customer asks for an email campaign. We might find the targeting is fine and the proposition is weak — in which case the right answer is research and proposition work before anybody writes a campaign.

freeAnalysis.metaDescription: Send us your customer list and we’ll analyse it through Education IQ — then an EdCo person will review the findings with you.
freeAnalysis.heroTitle: What don’t you know about your customers?
freeAnalysis.heroStandfirst: Send us your customer list. We’ll analyse it through Education IQ.
freeAnalysis.heroLead: Then an EdCo person reviews the findings with you. This is not an automated PDF report.
freeAnalysis.body: Most organisations know who their customers are. Rather fewer know what they have in common, which of them are at risk, or where the next twenty sit.
freeAnalysis.body3: A person who understands education looks at what came out, tells you what they think it means, and is prepared to disagree with you about it.
freeAnalysis.body4: What we need from you, what we do with it, and how long it takes.
freeAnalysis.heading: Somebody has already done this.

agencies.metaDescription: Bring EdCo into your team when you need specialist education capability. Your client stays your client.
agencies.heroTitle: You know your client. We know education.
agencies.heroLead: Bring EdCo into your team when you need specialist education capability. We can work visibly alongside you, under your brand, or quietly behind the scenes.
agencies.sectionTitle: And we bring other specialists in too
agencies.sectionLead: Where a piece of work needs expertise we don’t have, we’d rather find the right people than pretend.
agencies.ctaTitle: Got a client brief with education in it?
agencies.ctaBody: Tell us what your client is trying to achieve. We’ll tell you honestly whether we’re the right people, and what we’d bring.
agencies.heading: What you can bring us in for
agencies.body2: All of it, or one piece of it. White-label work is explicitly on the table — EdCo does not need to be the hero.
agencies.body4: We work alongside professional CSR agencies, marketing agencies and consultancies regularly. We are not trying to take ownership of your client relationship, and we’ll put that in writing if it helps.
agencies.heading2: Ask an agency we’ve worked with.

about.metaDescription: What we believe, how we got here and the people who do the work.
about.heroLead: We could open with a timeline. It seems more useful to tell you how we think, so you can work out whether you want us anywhere near your plans.
about.sectionLead: On top of that, EdCo has specialists in data, technology, research, marketing, content, events and strategy. And dedicated account managers whose job is to point that expertise at your objectives.
about.heading: We’ve been listening to educators since before email.
about.body: Channels have changed. Technology has changed. Education has changed almost beyond recognition.
about.body2: The need to understand educators before trying to engage them has not.
about.body3: Name, role, and one line on what they actually know about.
about.body5: You should have one relationship with EdCo, not separate relationships with several departments.
about.body6: Your Account Manager’s job isn’t to sell you whichever EdCo service happens to be next. It’s to understand what you’re trying to achieve and bring together the people who can help — then keep the work aligned to it, track progress, and challenge the assumptions when they need challenging.

contact.metaTitle: Tell us what you’re trying to achieve
contact.metaDescription: You don’t need to know which EdCo product or team you need. That’s our job.
contact.heroTitle: Tell us what you’re trying to achieve
contact.heroStandfirst: You don’t need to know which EdCo product or team you need. That’s our job.
contact.heroLead: Tell us what you’re trying to achieve and we’ll connect you with the right people.
contact.body: Choose as many as apply. Or none, if none of them fit.
contact.body2: Optional. As much or as little as you like.
contact.body3: Somebody who understands both education and your kind of organisation reads it, and gets in touch. Where it makes sense, that includes senior people.
contact.body4: We may well come back with a question rather than a proposal. That’s usually a good sign.
contact.heading: Already an EdCo customer?

customer.metaDescription: Logins and support for existing EdCo customers.
customer.body: If you’re an existing customer, everything you need is below. If you’d rather talk to a person, your account manager is the fastest route.
customer.heading: Your account manager
customer.body2: Your objectives become our objectives — and your account manager is the person who keeps it that way.

forEducators.metaDescription: Events, CPD, resources and research you can take part in — through the International Schools Network and The Curriculum Network.
forEducators.heroTitle: If you’re an educator, this bit is for you.
forEducators.heroStandfirst: We spend a lot of time asking educators what they need. Occasionally we have something to give back.
forEducators.heroLead: Most of this site is aimed at organisations that want to work with education. This part isn’t.
forEducators.sectionLead: Two communities EdCo runs, both free to join for educators.
forEducators.heading: Tell us what you’re dealing with
forEducators.body: We run interviews, focus groups and research studies with educators all year round. Sometimes they’re paid. Always they’re short, and we’ll tell you what we found.

whatWeThink.metaDescription: What we’re hearing from educators, what we think about it, and the research underneath.
whatWeThink.heroStandfirst: Worth knowing. Occasionally worth arguing about.
whatWeThink.heroLead: Three different things, kept deliberately separate: what the sector is telling us, what we think about it, and what the evidence actually says.
whatWeThink.ctaBody: Get the most useful things we’re hearing from educators, new research, EdCo opinion and invitations to events. No generic education-news roundup.

caseStudies.metaDescription: What organisations were trying to achieve, what we found, what we recommended and what changed.
caseStudies.heroTitle: What were they trying to achieve?
caseStudies.heroStandfirst: Every case study on this site answers the same seven questions.
caseStudies.heroLead: Including, in one or two of them, the awkward one: they asked us for X and we told them they needed Y.
caseStudies.heading: Eight to twelve substantial cases at launch
caseStudies.body: These are the themes the brief asks the launch set to cover. No case study goes live until the client facts, metrics and testimonial are verified and approved — nothing here is invented.

search.heading: Look for a theme, not a department.
search.body: SEND. MATs. School finance. Lead generation. Salesforce. Teacher workload. Whatever you’re dealing with — this searches everything we’ve published.

notFound.heading: That page isn’t here.
notFound.body: Which is annoying. Since you’re here anyway — what were you trying to achieve?
